findings.issue_text: [BUG] The new `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` redefines the previous four-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, so every existing caller that passes width and height as separate integers now hits the new signature. Any existing call like `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 100, 200)` binds dimensions=100 and opts=200; `opts[:allow_animation]` then calls Integer#[] with a Symbol and raises TypeError (`no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer`), and the generated geometry becomes `100` instead of `100x200` — thumbnail generation crashes for every post image.

[BUG] `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same path as both input and output for ImageMagick convert, which is not a safe in-place operation. `convert` opens the output file for writing before/while reading the input, so a same-path invocation truncates the source mid-read and produces a corrupted or zero-byte image (or a failed convert), after which `Upload.create_for` is handed a destroyed tempfile — large image uploads fail or store garbage.

[BUG] The animated-GIF branch in `optimize` dispatches on `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but the new controller call site passes a tempfile whose path is `discourse-upload-<type>/...` with no `.gif` extension. Animated GIFs uploaded through `create_upload` are downsized via the static-image instruction path; with `allow_animation` off that strips animation, and with the conversion flags differing from the animated path the output can be a broken/oversized first frame while the user believes their GIF was preserved.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop runs at most 5 iterations of an 80% scale and then falls through to `Upload.create_for` with no re-check that the file is now within `max_image_size_kb`. A pathological input (e.g., a large PNG that stays above the limit at 80%^5 ≈ 33% of original pixels, or a conversion failure) proceeds to upload over the limit, and the server-side validation rejects it with a generic error after the user waited through five full ImageMagick conversions — a slow failure path with no user feedback about why.

[ADVISORY] Hardcoding `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` on the client desynchronizes the client-side pre-check from the server's `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, which the diff deliberately still uses server-side (line 66 of uploads_controller.rb). When an admin sets max_image_size_kb to e.g. 1MB, the client happily passes a 5MB image; it then burns five synchronous ImageMagick downsizes on the server and, per the advisory above, may still be rejected or stored oversized — users see inconsistent limits between the alert text and actual behavior.

[BUG] The diff defines `def self.downsize` twice in the same module: the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` — Ruby silently keeps the last definition, so every existing caller that passes width and height as separate arguments now has `max_height` bound to `opts` and the string `'#{max_width}x#{max_height}'` is never built for them. Any out-of-diff caller invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 100, 200)` now passes `dimensions=100` (a bare number, not a `WxH` string) and `opts=200` (an Integer, not a Hash), producing broken imagemagick instructions or a TypeError — all existing thumbnail-generation paths that use the two-argument width/height form regress with no error at load time.

[BUG] The downsize loop is capped at 5 attempts (`attempt = 5 ... while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`) but there is no check after the loop that the file is actually under the limit — when 5 iterations of 80% geometric reduction are insufficient, execution falls through to `Upload.create_for` with an oversized file. A user uploads a very large image (or a PNG whose compressed size stays above the limit even after ~2.4x linear shrink); the loop exits without meeting the condition and the oversized file is passed to `Upload.create_for`, which then fails on the server-side size validation (or worse, bypasses validation depending on Upload's checks) instead of the promised automatic-reduction-to-allowed-size behavior — the PR's acceptance criterion (large images are reduced to allowed size) is silently dropped for this case.

[BUG] `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` downsizes in place and its return value (false when the `convert_with` backtick invocation exits nonzero) is ignored, so a failed imagemagick run leaves the tempfile unchanged and the loop retries the identical failing command up to 5 times before proceeding. When imagemagick fails on the input (corrupt/unsupported image, or in-place `from == to` overwriting the input mid-operation), the user gets either a corrupted upload or an unmodified oversized file passed to `Upload.create_for` — no error surfaces to the client and the wasted 5 shell invocations run on every matching upload.

[BUG] The client-side max-size check hardcodes `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` for every upload type, replacing the per-type `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup, so the gate no longer reflects the actual configured limits for composer, avatar, or any non-default setting. On any site configured with a limit under 10MB, users pass the client check and hit a server 413 — and the 413 handler (line 246) also hardcodes 10MB, so the reported max size in the `file_too_large` dialog is wrong on both paths; on a site configured above 10MB, the client now wrongly rejects files the server would accept.

[BUG] Two `def self.downsize` methods are defined in the same class body; the second (from, to, dimensions, opts) overrides the first (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts), so every caller still passing width/height separately raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). Any existing call site of OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h) — e.g. thumbnail generation paths in this same model that predate the refactor — crashes with ArgumentError, breaking image optimization site-wide.

[BUG] The downsize loop passes the same path as both `from` and `to` (`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`), but convert_with shells out to ImageMagick which cannot safely read and write the identical file in one command. The convert command either fails (exitstatus != 0, silently swallowed since the return value is ignored) leaving the oversized file to be rejected, or produces a corrupt/truncated image that is then stored; either way the promised 'automatically downsize large images' behavior never happens for any user.

[BUG] The loop gives up after 5 attempts of 80% (min achievable ≈ 33% of original size), so images larger than ~3× max_image_size_kb exit the loop still over the limit and proceed to Upload.create_for, which rejects them with an error the user cannot fix. Users uploading e.g. a 40MB image to a 5MB-limit site get a hard rejection with no downsizing, defeating the feature's stated intent for exactly the large files it targets.

[BUG] The per-type site setting check `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` is replaced with a hardcoded 10MB constant, silently ignoring admin-configured limits for all upload types (images, attachments, banners). Admins who set max_image_size_kb above 10MB see uploads blocked at 10MB client-side with no explanation; admins who set it below 10MB get client-side acceptance of files the server then rejects for non-images (server downsizing only applies to images), breaking the contract for attachments.

[BUG] The 413 handler hardcodes 10MB, desynchronizing the client error message from the server's actual configured max_image_size_kb. Users who hit the server's real limit (e.g. 2MB) are shown an alert claiming the max is 10MB, prompting retries that always fail — the displayed requirement is false.

[ADVISORY] The API-URL download size cap is hardcoded to 10.megabytes instead of the per-call site setting, an unrelated behavioral change not traceable to the 'downsize large images' requirement. API consumers on sites with a configured limit above 10MB can no longer pull remote files larger than 10MB via URL upload; this change is invisible to admins and unrelated to the feature.

[ADVISORY] The downsizing operates on the raw tempfile before Upload.create_for records the original size, and the original bytes are permanently destroyed with no retention of the pre-downsize file, an unstated data-loss behavior not covered by any requirement in the PR title. Users who upload a high-resolution original lose it irrecoverably (the upload record stores only the shrunk copy's size); a later 'download original' or lightbox zoom shows the degraded 33%-quality image with no indication the original existed.

[BUG] The downsize loop runs at most 5 iterations of '80%' (best case ~32.8% of original) and then falls through to Upload.create anyway, so an image starting at >3x the allowed size is never reduced enough and is still created at full size. A user uploads a 40MB image with max_image_size_kb=10000: after 5 passes the file is still ~13MB, the loop exits via the attempt counter, and Upload.create_for runs on the still-oversized tempfile — the size limit the loop was added to enforce is silently not enforced.

[BUG] The '80%' argument is passed as the `dimensions` parameter of OptimizedImage.downsize, whose instructions methods expect a 'WxH' geometry string and interpolate it into ImageMagick geometry math, not a percentage. downsize_instructions builds crop/geometry strings from the '80%' value (or ImageMagick -downsize rejects a bare percentage, which -resize accepts but -downsize does not), so the conversion either fails with a nonzero exitstatus (silently ignored since convert_with only returns false and the caller ignores the result) or produces wrong geometry, and the loop's condition never converges predictably.

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is called with from == to (tempfile.path for both), and the underlying convert pipeline reads the input file and writes the output file — in-place conversion overwrites the input while it is being read. ImageMagick/gifsicle commands generated by convert_with write to `to` mid-read of `from`; on the same path this truncates or corrupts the image (or fails outright), so the 'automatically reduced' image is a 0-byte/garbage file that is then stored via Upload.create_for.

[BUG] The client-side max size check is hardcoded to 10*1024 KB, replacing SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the per-type site settings are no longer consulted and the value now diverges from the server's enforcement. Admins who raise max_image_size_kb above 10MB (or lower it) get a client that rejects uploads the server would accept (or accepts ones the server rejects with a confusing 413), and the type-specific settings (avatar vs composer) are silently dead on the client.

[ADVISORY] The download size cap for API URL uploads is hardcoded to 10.megabytes, parallel to the 10*1024 constant in utilities.js, duplicating in two places a limit that is also drifting from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb used two lines later. The next editor who changes one copy (JS or Ruby) leaves the other behind, and the two already disagree with the site setting the rest of the diff enforces; also SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb < 10MB sites now download 10MB files only to downsize them.

[ADVISORY] The class now defines `def self.downsize` twice — the new string-joining version shadows the first definition, leaving the earlier one as dead code that the next reader will assume is the live one. A future edit to the first definition (the one matching the resize/downsize signature symmetry) has no effect because Ruby silently uses the last definition, making the next change to this file riskier and harder to reason about.

[ADVISORY] After the downsize loop, the upload is created with the ORIGINAL tempfile.size argument captured before... actually tempfile.size is re-evaluated, but content_type is the original declared type while the file may have been re-encoded, and the record's size is read from a possibly corrupted in-place-downsized file with no verification that the downsize succeeded (convert_with's false return is ignored). If convert_with fails (bad geometry, missing convert binary, in-place write failure), the loop silently burns all 5 attempts on an unchanged or truncated file and Upload.create_for persists whatever remains — users get broken/oversized images stored with a success response.

[BUG] The client file-size check replaces the admin-configurable SiteSetting max_<type>_size_kb with a hardcoded 10MB constant, silently discarding the accepted behavior that upload limits are site-configurable. Admins who set max_image_size_kb below 10MB get users shown 'file too large' at the wrong threshold, and admins who raise it above 10MB are silently capped at 10MB client-side; the feature changed the objective (configurable limit -> fixed limit) without any acceptance of that constraint change.

[BUG] The 413 error handler hardcodes 10MB instead of reading SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, so the error message reports a size limit unrelated to what the server actually enforces. When the server rejects an upload with 413 at the configured limit (e.g. 2MB), the user is told the limit is 10MB, producing a message that contradicts the server's real behavior and misdirects the user.

[BUG] The client-side check now blocks files over 10MB before the server's new auto-downsize path can shrink them, directly contradicting the feature intent of 'automatically downsize large images'. An image of 12MB is rejected in the browser with 'file too large' even though the server-side loop at uploads_controller.rb was written to downsize it, so the advertised feature is unreachable for files between 10MB and the downsize ceiling, blocking the feature's core intent.

[BUG] The diff defines self.downsize twice — once as (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) and again as (from, to, dimensions, opts) — and in Ruby the second definition replaces the first, so all existing callers passing max_width and max_height as separate arguments now pass max_height where opts is expected. Any pre-existing call site like OptimizedImage.downsize(path, out, 690, 690) executes with dimensions=690 and opts=690 (not a Hash), so opts[...] lookups raise TypeError (nil implicit conversion / no implicit conversion into Integer) or produce corrupt geometry strings, breaking every existing thumbnail generation path outside this diff.

[BUG] The downsize loop passes the string "80%" as the dimensions argument to OptimizedImage.downsize, which forwards it into downsize_instructions expecting a WxH geometry, and '80%' is not a valid WxH dimensions string for those instruction builders. The conversion command is built with an invalid geometry, convert exits non-zero, convert_with returns false, and the loop blindly retries five times before Upload.create_for is called with an un-shrunk oversized tempfile, so the 'automatically downsize' feature never actually downsizes and large uploads fail at Upload.create's size validation.

[ADVISORY] FileHelper.download's max-size bound is hardcoded to 10.megabytes, silently removing the SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb bound for API-provided URLs instead of applying the new downsize path to them. Operators who configured a lower max_image_size_kb as a cost/bandwidth control lose that control for API URL downloads, and downloads now proceed up to 10MB regardless of site configuration — a silent constraint change shipped without a setting update or migration.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop ignores the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize/convert_with (which returns false on convert failure) and loops up to five fixed iterations with no convergence guarantee. A pathological or already-small-but-slightly-over image can burn five sequential convert invocations on the request thread and still be over the limit, then fall through to Upload.create_for with an oversized file, yielding a confusing server error after seconds of CPU burn; the original intent (accept large images gracefully) fails silently.

[BUG] The admin-configurable size control SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb is replaced with a hardcoded 10.megabytes cap on server-side URL downloads, so operators can no longer tighten the download limit below 10MB. On a site where max_image_size_kb is set to e.g. 256KB, an API caller can still force the server to download and buffer up to 10MB per request from an arbitrary URL, reintroducing an admin-configured bandwidth/DoS limit the site relied on; the setting silently stops being enforced on this path.

[ADVISORY] The client-side upload check now reports a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of the site's configured max_<type>_size_kb, so the client enforcement is decoupled from the server's configured control. Admins who lower max_image_size_kb get client-side uploads that pass the 10MB gate and then fail server-side with a generic error, and admins who raise it above 10MB get users blocked from legitimate uploads; the security control (upload size cap as DoS guard) is no longer tunable from the surface users actually hit.

[ADVISORY] The new downsize loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) using the same path as source and destination, in-place mutating the uploaded bytes before any validation by Upload.create_for. When ImageMagick fails or produces a zero-byte/corrupt output writing in-place (from and to are the same file), a corrupted tempfile is handed to Upload.create_for and the run-loop's 5 iterations silently exit with an oversized or empty file still being processed, so upload validation operates on mutated attacker-supplied bytes rather than what was originally uploaded; the failure is silent because exit status of the in-place convert is only checked in convert_with's return value which this loop ignores.

[BUG] def self.downsize is defined twice in the same class body, so the second (3-arg dimensions-string) definition silently replaces the first (max_width/max_height) definition and every existing 4-arg+opts caller of downsize now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). Any pre-existing call site like OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 1024, 768) — the existing thumbnail-generation paths — raises ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 4, expected 3), breaking all thumbnail generation; the diff adds zero tests, so this latent breakage ships undetected.

[BUG] The new downsizing loop passes "80%" as the dimensions argument and never checks the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize, which convert_with returns false from on ImageMagick failure, so the loop happily spins 5 times on an un-shrunk file and then calls Upload.create_for with the still-oversized tempfile.size. For a corrupt or non-shrinkable oversized image (or any convert failure), the upload proceeds with the original oversized size and fails server-side with the generic 'file too large' path the loop was meant to eliminate; no test in the diff exercises the failed-downsize branch or the 5-iteration cap, so the loop's exit conditions (success vs. exhausted attempts vs. convert error) are all unverified.

[BUG] The guard uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename) on the downloaded-URL path where filename is File.basename(URI.parse(url).path), but for multipart uploads the check is on filename only, and the loop downsizes in place on tempfile.path while ImageMagick animates GIFs when allow_animation is passed — yet no test in the diff triggers the animated-GIF branch (downsize_instructions_animated via opts[:allow_animation] and the \.GIF$ regex on from) for this new call site. The animated-GIF path of the new loop (which routes to downsize_instructions_animated and passes "80%" through a different instructions builder that may not accept a bare percentage) is never exercised; if its instruction builder chokes on "80%" the whole upload of a large GIF 500s, a regression only users uploading large animated images will hit.

[ADVISORY] The client hardcodes the 10MB limit while the server still gates on SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, and no spec change in this diff pins the client-side maxSizeKB constant or the 413-path message content, so the displayed 'max size' can now contradict what the server actually enforces. Operators who set max_image_size_kb below 10MB see uploads rejected server-side with a message claiming 10MB is allowed; any future change to the setting drifts silently because nothing asserts the client/server limit agreement.

[BUG] `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined twice in the same class body (the original 4-argument version and a new 3-argument `dimensions` version), so Ruby's last-definition-wins silently replaces the 4-argument method and every existing caller that still passes width and height as separate integers (e.g. the thumbnail-generation paths that call downsize with `width, height`) now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). All pre-existing image thumbnail/downsize call sites in the app that were not updated in this diff crash with ArgumentError, breaking avatar/theme-component thumbnail generation for every upload until the callers are migrated to the new signature.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop ignores the boolean return of OptimizedImage.downsize/convert_with and has no check after the loop, so a tempfile whose ImageMagick conversion failed (exitstatus != 0, possibly leaving the in-place output path `tempfile.path` truncated/corrupted since from == to) or that is still above max_image_size_kb after 5 attempts is passed to Upload.create_for unconditionally. A user uploading an image that ImageMagick cannot downsize (huge dimensions, corrupt input) gets a corrupted or still-oversized file silently stored/served as their upload instead of the original bytes or a clear error — silent data loss of the uploaded original and a server-side size limit that can still be exceeded.

[ADVISORY] The client-side check replaces the site-configurable `SiteSetting['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded 10 * 1024, so the client tells users '10MB' regardless of the actual server limit set by the operator. On sites where an admin has set max_image_size_kb below 10MB, users see a 'too large' message quoting 10MB and, for files between the real limit and 10MB, only learn of the failure via a raw 413 from the server instead of the intended client-side message; conversely the message lies about the limit the server enforces.

[BUG] The downsize loop (lines 63-70) ignores the boolean return of OptimizedImage.downsize (which returns false when the ImageMagick convert exits non-zero) and also never checks whether the file actually shrank below SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes after 5 attempts, then unconditionally proceeds to Upload.create_for with the still-oversized or corrupted file. When convert_with fails (e.g. '80%' produces invalid -resize syntax for downsize_instructions, or the image cannot be compressed below the limit like a small-dimension PNG or a large animated GIF), the user gets a confusing 413/500 from create_for instead of a clear 'could not resize' error, and a file that failed 5 converts in a row is silently re-uploaded possibly corrupted by a partial in-place write.

[BUG] The new 3-arg downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) signature collides with every existing caller that invokes the old 4-argument form downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts): the old max_width is consumed as the dimensions string and the old max_height integer is consumed as the opts hash, producing malformed ImageMagick instructions. Any in-tree caller still passing width and height separately (e.g. thumbnail-generation code paths) now generates instructions like '-resize W' with the opts hash discarded, so thumbnails silently come out with the wrong dimensions or convert fails with exitstatus != 0 whose return is unhandled — a runtime regression on the thumbnail path.

[BUG] When FileHelper.download fails, the 'rescue nil' leaves tempfile nil and content_type nil, yet execution falls through to Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, ...) with a nil tempfile, raising NoMethodError (nil.size) and returning a 500 instead of the 4xx the API contract promises for a bad URL. API users POSTing an unreachable URL get a raw 500 (NoMethodError on nil) instead of a validation error naming the URL, and the failure is logged as an app error rather than a client error.

[ADVISORY] The client-side size check and the 413 handler hardcode 10MB while the server enforces SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb (and now downsizes oversized images), so the error message the user sees names a limit the server no longer applies and rejects client-side uploads the server would have accepted and auto-resized. Users on sites with max_image_size_kb < 10MB are told 'too large' with a wrong 10MB figure, and users with images between max_image_size_kb and 10MB are blocked client-side even though the server would now downsize and accept them.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated branch is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. The new controller logic calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`, where `from` is a tempfile path (e.g., `file.tempfile.path` or `FileHelper.download(...)` result). Tempfile paths commonly do not preserve the original `.gif` extension, so the regex check can fail even for animated GIF uploads, causing the non-animated instruction path to be used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The downsize loop runs at most 5 iterations of an 80% scale and then falls through to `Upload.create_for` with no re-check that the file is now within `max_image_size_kb`. A pathological input (e.g., a large PNG that stays above the limit at 80%^5 ≈ 33% of original pixels, or a conversion failure) proceeds to upload over the limit, and the server-side validation rejects it with a generic error after the user waited through five full ImageMagick conversions — a slow failure path with no user feedback about why.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new image-reduction loop (`attempt = 5; while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes ... OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`) has no explicit post-loop check that `tempfile.size` is now <= the limit before calling `Upload.create_for(...)`. So if downsizing fails to reduce enough (or fails silently), the request still pays up to 5 conversions and then relies on later validation/error handling, which can lead to a slow failure path with unclear user feedback. The diff does not show that this bypasses limits, just that it may waste work before rejection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Hardcoding `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` on the client desynchronizes the client-side pre-check from the server's `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, which the diff deliberately still uses server-side (line 66 of uploads_controller.rb). When an admin sets max_image_size_kb to e.g. 1MB, the client happily passes a 5MB image; it then burns five synchronous ImageMagick downsizes on the server and, per the advisory above, may still be rejected or stored oversized — users see inconsistent limits between the alert text and actual behavior.

[BUG] The diff defines `def self.downsize` twice in the same module: the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` — Ruby silently keeps the last definition, so every existing caller that passes width and height as separate arguments now has `max_height` bound to `opts` and the string `'#{max_width}x#{max_height}'` is never built for them. Any out-of-diff caller invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 100, 200)` now passes `dimensions=100` (a bare number, not a `WxH` string) and `opts=200` (an Integer, not a Hash), producing broken imagemagick instructions or a TypeError — all existing thumbnail-generation paths that use the two-argument width/height form regress with no error at load time.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, the diff leaves an existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then adds another `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` later. Ruby does not overload methods by arity; the later definition replaces the earlier one. Any existing call sites using the 4-argument form (e.g. `downsize(from,to,100,200)`) will now be interpreted as `dimensions=100, opts=200`, and `optimize` immediately does `opts[:allow_animation]`, which will raise (Integer doesn’t support `[]`) or otherwise generate invalid instructions. This is a real behavioral regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop is capped at 5 attempts (`attempt = 5 ... while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`) but there is no check after the loop that the file is actually under the limit — when 5 iterations of 80% geometric reduction are insufficient, execution falls through to `Upload.create_for` with an oversized file. A user uploads a very large image (or a PNG whose compressed size stays above the limit even after ~2.4x linear shrink); the loop exits without meeting the condition and the oversized file is passed to `Upload.create_for`, which then fails on the server-side size validation (or worse, bypasses validation depending on Upload's checks) instead of the promised automatic-reduction-to-allowed-size behavior — the PR's acceptance criterion (large images are reduced to allowed size) is silently dropped for this case.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new downsizing loop (`attempt = 5 ... while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`) can terminate because `attempt` reaches 0 while `tempfile.size` is still above the limit, and there is no post-loop check/handling before calling `Upload.create_for(...)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` downsizes in place and its return value (false when the `convert_with` backtick invocation exits nonzero) is ignored, so a failed imagemagick run leaves the tempfile unchanged and the loop retries the identical failing command up to 5 times before proceeding. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The downsize loop ignores the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize/convert_with (which returns false on convert failure) and loops up to five fixed iterations with no convergence guarantee. A pathological or already-small-but-slightly-over image can burn five sequential convert invocations on the request thread and still be over the limit, then fall through to Upload.create_for with an oversized file, yielding a confusing server error after seconds of CPU burn; the original intent (accept large images gracefully) fails silently.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times but ignores its boolean return value (in `optimized_image.rb`, `optimize` returns `convert_with(...)`, which returns `false` on conversion failure). The loop also stops after a fixed 5 iterations even if `tempfile.size` remains above `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, then proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` with the still-oversized `tempfile.size`, potentially causing a later rejection/error after spending CPU time on repeated conversions. This is a diff-introduced correctness/behavior issue in the new “auto-reduce” upload path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The admin-configurable size control SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb is replaced with a hardcoded 10.megabytes cap on server-side URL downloads, so operators can no longer tighten the download limit below 10MB. On a site where max_image_size_kb is set to e.g. 256KB, an API caller can still force the server to download and buffer up to 10MB per request from an arbitrary URL, reintroducing an admin-configured bandwidth/DoS limit the site relied on; the setting silently stops being enforced on this path.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb, the API URL-download path changes `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`, removing enforcement of the admin-configured `max_image_size_kb` for server-side URL downloads. The later downsize loop applies only after the tempfile has already been downloaded, so it does not prevent downloading/buffering up to 10MB even if the setting is smaller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The client-side upload check now reports a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of the site's configured max_<type>_size_kb, so the client enforcement is decoupled from the server's configured control. Admins who lower max_image_size_kb get client-side uploads that pass the 10MB gate and then fail server-side with a generic error, and admins who raise it above 10MB get users blocked from legitimate uploads; the security control (upload size cap as DoS guard) is no longer tunable from the surface users actually hit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the client-side max size checks in `utilities.js` from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in both the pre-upload validation and the 413 handler. This verifiably decouples client enforcement/messaging from the server-configured limits, causing mismatches when admins configure limits below or above 10MB (client may allow then server rejects, or client blocks allowed uploads).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new downsize loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) using the same path as source and destination, in-place mutating the uploaded bytes before any validation by Upload.create_for. When ImageMagick fails or produces a zero-byte/corrupt output writing in-place (from and to are the same file), a corrupted tempfile is handed to Upload.create_for and the run-loop's 5 iterations silently exit with an oversized or empty file still being processed, so upload validation operates on mutated attacker-supplied bytes rather than what was originally uploaded; the failure is silent because exit status of the in-place convert is only checked in convert_with's return value which this loop ignores.

adjudication.rationale: The added loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, using the same path for input and output, so it mutates the uploaded tempfile in-place before `Upload.create_for` runs. The conversion helper (`OptimizedImage.convert_with`) only signals failure via its return value (`false` on nonzero exit), but the loop ignores any return value, so a failed/partial in-place conversion can leave an oversized, empty, or otherwise corrupted tempfile that is still passed to `Upload.create_for` with the mutated `tempfile.size`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] def self.downsize is defined twice in the same class body, so the second (3-arg dimensions-string) definition silently replaces the first (max_width/max_height) definition and every existing 4-arg+opts caller of downsize now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). Any pre-existing call site like OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 1024, 768) — the existing thumbnail-generation paths — raises ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 4, expected 3), breaking all thumbnail generation; the diff adds zero tests, so this latent breakage ships undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, `def self.downsize` is defined twice: first as `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and later as `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby, the second definition overwrites the first, so any existing callers passing four positional args (e.g., `downsize(from, to, 1024, 768, ...)` or `downsize(from, to, 1024, 768)`) will now raise `ArgumentError` due to the new arity. This is a concrete defect introduced by the diff regardless of whether call sites are shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new downsizing loop passes "80%" as the dimensions argument and never checks the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize, which convert_with returns false from on ImageMagick failure, so the loop happily spins 5 times on an un-shrunk file and then calls Upload.create_for with the still-oversized tempfile.size. For a corrupt or non-shrinkable oversized image (or any convert failure), the upload proceeds with the original oversized size and fails server-side with the generic 'file too large' path the loop was meant to eliminate; no test in the diff exercises the failed-downsize branch or the 5-iteration cap, so the loop's exit conditions (success vs. exhausted attempts vs. convert error) are all unverified.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but ignores its return value. In `optimized_image.rb`, `optimize` returns `convert_with(...)`, which returns `false` on ImageMagick failure. If downsizing fails (corrupt image/convert error), `tempfile.size` won’t change, so the `while` condition stays true and the code will retry up to 5 times and then still call `Upload.create_for(...)` with the oversized `tempfile.size`, defeating the intended auto-reduction path and adding redundant work. (Passing "80%" is consistent with the new `downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts)` signature, so that part isn’t clearly wrong from the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The guard uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename) on the downloaded-URL path where filename is File.basename(URI.parse(url).path), but for multipart uploads the check is on filename only, and the loop downsizes in place on tempfile.path while ImageMagick animates GIFs when allow_animation is passed — yet no test in the diff triggers the animated-GIF branch (downsize_instructions_animated via opts[:allow_animation] and the \.GIF$ regex on from) for this new call site. The animated-GIF path of the new loop (which routes to downsize_instructions_animated and passes "80%" through a different instructions builder that may not accept a bare percentage) is never exercised; if its instruction builder chokes on "80%" the whole upload of a large GIF 500s, a regression only users uploading large animated images will hit.
matched_golden_ids: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core bug: when the animated-GIF code path is used (allow_animated_thumbnails/allow_animation), the resize instruction "80%" is passed to the animated resizing backend (e.g., gifsicle --resize-fit) which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage, so the resize will not work (silently or via error). The candidate adds context about test coverage and potential 500s, but the underlying issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The client hardcodes the 10MB limit while the server still gates on SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, and no spec change in this diff pins the client-side maxSizeKB constant or the 413-path message content, so the displayed 'max size' can now contradict what the server actually enforces. Operators who set max_image_size_kb below 10MB see uploads rejected server-side with a message claiming 10MB is allowed; any future change to the setting drifts silently because nothing asserts the client/server limit agreement.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the client-side max size checks were changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in both the pre-upload validation and the 413 error handler. On the server, the logic still references `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (e.g., the new downsize loop only targets `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, and non-image uploads are not covered by that loop), so installations with limits != 10MB can see client-side acceptance / messaging diverge from what the server will actually accept. This is a real behavior regression introduced by the diff, not just a test concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined twice in the same class body (the original 4-argument version and a new 3-argument `dimensions` version), so Ruby's last-definition-wins silently replaces the 4-argument method and every existing caller that still passes width and height as separate integers (e.g. the thumbnail-generation paths that call downsize with `width, height`) now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). All pre-existing image thumbnail/downsize call sites in the app that were not updated in this diff crash with ArgumentError, breaking avatar/theme-component thumbnail generation for every upload until the callers are migrated to the new signature.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, `def self.downsize` is defined twice: first with signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, then later redefined as `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby will silently keep only the last definition, so any existing call sites still passing `max_width, max_height` as separate args will raise `ArgumentError` (wrong number of arguments). This is a real defect introduced by the diff regardless of whether call sites were updated elsewhere (not shown here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The downsize loop ignores the boolean return of OptimizedImage.downsize/convert_with and has no check after the loop, so a tempfile whose ImageMagick conversion failed (exitstatus != 0, possibly leaving the in-place output path `tempfile.path` truncated/corrupted since from == to) or that is still above max_image_size_kb after 5 attempts is passed to Upload.create_for unconditionally. A user uploading an image that ImageMagick cannot downsize (huge dimensions, corrupt input) gets a corrupted or still-oversized file silently stored/served as their upload instead of the original bytes or a clear error — silent data loss of the uploaded original and a server-side size limit that can still be exceeded.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` up to 5 times but never checks its return value and never verifies post-conditions before calling `Upload.create_for(...)`. In optimized_image.rb, `convert_with` returns `false` when ImageMagick fails (`exitstatus != 0`), and otherwise returns `nil`, so failures are silently ignored. Because the conversion is done in-place (`from == to`), a failed/partial conversion can leave `tempfile` corrupted, and if size remains above `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` after 5 attempts it is still uploaded unconditionally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The client-side check replaces the site-configurable `SiteSetting['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded 10 * 1024, so the client tells users '10MB' regardless of the actual server limit set by the operator. On sites where an admin has set max_image_size_kb below 10MB, users see a 'too large' message quoting 10MB and, for files between the real limit and 10MB, only learn of the failure via a raw 413 from the server instead of the intended client-side message; conversely the message lies about the limit the server enforces.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the client-side configurable limit (`Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`) with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` in two places in `utilities.js`, so the client’s preflight check and 413 error message will always use 10MB regardless of the actual site settings. This can mislead users and cause files that exceed the real server limit but are <10MB to bypass the intended client-side rejection and only fail server-side.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop (lines 63-70) ignores the boolean return of OptimizedImage.downsize (which returns false when the ImageMagick convert exits non-zero) and also never checks whether the file actually shrank below SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes after 5 attempts, then unconditionally proceeds to Upload.create_for with the still-oversized or corrupted file. When convert_with fails (e.g. '80%' produces invalid -resize syntax for downsize_instructions, or the image cannot be compressed below the limit like a small-dimension PNG or a large animated GIF), the user gets a confusing 413/500 from create_for instead of a clear 'could not resize' error, and a file that failed 5 converts in a row is silently re-uploaded possibly corrupted by a partial in-place write.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times but ignores its boolean return (optimized_image.rb `convert_with` returns false on non-zero exit). After the loop it also does not check `tempfile.size` against `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` before proceeding to `Upload.create_for`, so an unresized/oversized (or potentially partially modified) tempfile can be uploaded and then fail later with a less clear error. These behaviors are directly visible in the added loop and the return contract in OptimizedImage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new 3-arg downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) signature collides with every existing caller that invokes the old 4-argument form downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts): the old max_width is consumed as the dimensions string and the old max_height integer is consumed as the opts hash, producing malformed ImageMagick instructions. Any in-tree caller still passing width and height separately (e.g. thumbnail-generation code paths) now generates instructions like '-resize W' with the opts hash discarded, so thumbnails silently come out with the wrong dimensions or convert fails with exitstatus != 0 whose return is unhandled — a runtime regression on the thumbnail path.

adjudication.rationale: In `optimized_image.rb`, `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is immediately followed by another `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby does not overload by arity, so the later definition replaces the former. Any existing callers still using the old `(from,to,max_width,max_height,opts)` form will now either raise an argument error (5 args) or pass `max_height` into `opts`, causing `opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` to misbehave/raise (since `opts` is not a Hash) and/or generate wrong convert instructions. This is a real runtime regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When FileHelper.download fails, the 'rescue nil' leaves tempfile nil and content_type nil, yet execution falls through to Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, ...) with a nil tempfile, raising NoMethodError (nil.size) and returning a 500 instead of the 4xx the API contract promises for a bad URL. API users POSTing an unreachable URL get a raw 500 (NoMethodError on nil) instead of a validation error naming the URL, and the failure is logged as an app error rather than a client error.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the API URL branch sets `tempfile = FileHelper.download(...) rescue nil` and does not set `content_type`. If the download fails, `tempfile` is `nil` and the new downsize block is skipped due to `if tempfile && ...`, but execution still reaches `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)`. Calling `tempfile.size` when `tempfile` is `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 rather than a client error for a bad/unreachable URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The client-side size check and the 413 handler hardcode 10MB while the server enforces SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb (and now downsizes oversized images), so the error message the user sees names a limit the server no longer applies and rejects client-side uploads the server would have accepted and auto-resized. Users on sites with max_image_size_kb < 10MB are told 'too large' with a wrong 10MB figure, and users with images between max_image_size_kb and 10MB are blocked client-side even though the server would now downsize and accept them.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js` the client-side size check and the 413 handler were changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings[...]` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB (10MB). Meanwhile on the server (`uploads_controller.rb`) oversized images are explicitly handled relative to `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` by downsizing in a loop before `Upload.create_for`. This creates a real mismatch: the UI will report/assume a 10MB limit regardless of site settings, and will block any upload >10MB even though the server-side logic may now accept larger images by downsizing them to the configured limit. Also, for non-image types, the client no longer reflects `max_{type}_size_kb` at all, potentially allowing files the server would reject or rejecting files the server would allow if settings differ from 10MB.
